Previously nonlit Rep decomposition returned bytes directly without multiplying/copying full pattern? For each read of small line, old read_range Rep nonlit could extract partial pattern with no full copy. Also fast header buffer reads chunks, cache maybe copies pattern each read. But likely not huge. We should revert cache or optimize use of pattern_data multiplication. For each read requested take (chunk up to maybe1024), if pattern_data p658 and offset maybe, `repeats=(offset+needed+p-1)//p`, often2, data=pattern_data*2 ~1316, slice; okay. 3 reads per request ~4k copies vs old. Maybe cache memory and branch slows. 20k overhead. Could leave; performance15 under20 borderline. Better revert cache to reduce risk and complexity. But maybe for larger header block cache helps? Yet observed worse. Revert only cache addition, keep `_Rep` slots harmless. Could remove `_small` and branch. We'll revert to old Rep branch. Use Python script.
